results.notes: Official product page: https://audiogroupdenmark.com/product/aavik-i-280/. The brand domain aavik-acoustics.com 301-redirects to audiogroupdenmark.com — Audio Group Denmark is Aavik's own parent/manufacturer, so audiogroupdenmark.com IS the official manufacturer domain (not a retailer or third party); all images are served from its wp-content/uploads. onOfficialDomain=true for all. Image URLs were extracted from og:image / JSON-LD thumbnailUrl and the page tags. The og:image points to '4K_AAVIK_I-280_LANDINGPAGE-scaled.jpg' but I substituted the un-suffixed original '4K_AAVIK_I-280_LANDINGPAGE.jpg' after confirming via curl -I that it returns HTTP 200, image/jpeg, and is ~9x larger (1.02 MB vs 117 KB) than the scaled version. All four URLs HEAD-verified as HTTP 200 with image/* content-type and substantial size. Header/logo/sprite images and images belonging to sibling models (I-580, R-880, etc.) were excluded.

The official manufacturer site accusticarts.de is fully reachable (homepage HTTP 200) and NOT blocked, but there is NO "Reference Rack" product anywhere on it. Verified by: (1) fetching the homepage and /produkte/ product index; (2) parsing the WordPress Yoast sitemap index and full page-sitemap.xml (every product URL listed); (3) scanning post-sitemap and attachment-sitemap (90 media items). Every AccusticArts product is electronics — CD players (PLAYER I-IV), DACs (TUBE-DAC II), preamps, power/mono/stereo amplifiers (AMP/MONO/POWER), transports (DRIVE). No equipment rack, stand, or "Reference Rack" exists. Slug probes (reference-rack, rack, racks, referenzrack, zubehoer, reference-rack-ii) all 404'd, and no sitemap loc, product link, attachment, or on-page text matches rack/reference/regal/stand. Per strict source rules I did NOT substitute any third-party source. Conclusion: "Acoustic Arts Reference Rack" does not exist as a product on the official accusticarts.de domain, so no official product image could be retrieved. Likely a catalog/brand-mapping error upstream — recommend verifying the product name.

results.notes:
Official domain confirmed reachable and authoritative, but NOT directly fetchable from this environment: borresen-acoustics.com is behind Cloudflare (162.159.135.42) which rejects every TLS ClientHello from all local clients with fatal alert 40 (handshake_failure) — verified across Schannel curl (SEC_E_ILLEGAL_MESSAGE), OpenSSL-based WebFetch (HANDSHAKE_FAILURE_ON_CLIENT_HELLO), .NET Invoke-WebRequest, and openssl s_client (TLS1.3 group NULL). This is a bot/TLS-fingerprint block, not a site outage — Google (WebSearch) and the Wayback Machine reach it fine. The built-in Browser pane is scoped to the local dev server (external nav denied) and the Claude-in-Chrome extension is not connected, so no real browser was available. r.jina.ai reader was 403/422 rate-limited.

Discovery method: I recovered the official product page's own HTML from the Wayback Machine (latest 200 snapshot 20220119165356, raw id_ replay) and extracted image URLs directly from it. All URLs returned are authentic paths referenced by the official page and resolve to the manufacturer's own domain (borresen-acoustics.com/images/...). REJECTED nothing from third parties.

Caveats: (1) The /images/ asset files themselves were never archived by Wayback (archive.org availability API returns no snapshots), so I could NOT byte-verify content-type or pixel dimensions for the two main images — content types are inferred from file extension. The SILVER_238px badge WAS archived and confirmed image/png. (2) Børresen markets "Silver Supreme" as a premium edition/finish of each 0-series model, not a distinct SKU with its own page — the canonical official page for the model is the standard 05 page, so borresen_05_goldenear.jpg is the best available official product image of the physical speaker. A live re-fetch from a client with a modern browser TLS fingerprint (real Chrome) is recommended to byte-confirm and pull any higher-res/current hero, since the page may have been redesigned since the 2022 archive.
